challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: Human Dignity and Liberty (1992)
challenged.gazette: ס״ח 1391, 25 March 1992, p. 150 (issue number and page from memory, not re-verified this session)
challenged.case: CA 6821/93 United Mizrahi Bank Ltd. v. Migdal Cooperative Village (with LCA 1908/94, LCA 3363/94), IsrSC 49(4) 221
challenged.panel_and_vote: Nine justices (Shamgar P. (ret.), Barak P., D. Levin, Bach, Goldberg, Mazza, Cheshin, Zamir, Tal). Basic Laws held to be supra-legislative and binding by 8–1 (Cheshin dissenting on the constituent-authority theory; Shamgar reaching supremacy via unlimited Knesset sovereignty); the attacked ordinary statute (Family Agricultural Sector (Arrangements) (Amendment) Law 1993) upheld unanimously as consistent with s. 8.
challenged.source: https://versa.cardozo.yu.edu/opinions/united-mizrahi-bank-v-migdal-cooperative-village ; cited by Hayut in HCJ 5658/23 paras 52–55 (https://versa.cardozo.yu.edu/node/705)
challenged.note: Not a petition attacking the Basic Law's validity; included (per the brief) because the Court decided the Basic Law's binding force / supremacy over later ordinary legislation, which the debtors' side and Cheshin J. contested. Hayut (5658/23 para 52–55) treats Mizrahi as the origin of the 'form test' for identifying Basic Laws.

challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: Freedom of Occupation (1994 re-enactment, including the s. 8 override clause and s. 10)
challenged.gazette: ס״ח 1454, 10 March 1994, p. 90 (issue number and page from memory, not re-verified this session)
challenged.case: HCJ 1368/94 Shay Porat v. State of Israel, IsrSC 57(5) 913 (1994)
challenged.source: Hayut, HCJ 5658/23 para 92 (Versa node 705, reference [58]): cited for the proposition that 'the constitutionality of Basic Laws cannot be reviewed in accordance with the tests set out in the limitation clause'; Yaniv Roznai, Maariv op-ed 13 Nov 2020 (https://www.maariv.co.il/journalists/opinions/article-801969): 'in 1994 the Court heard a petition asking it to declare Basic Law: Freedom of Occupation void and dismissed it without addressing the problems of judicial review of Basic Laws'
challenged.note: Identification rests on two secondary references; full text not reached (Nevo/supremedecisions not fetched). The 1994 petition described by Roznai matches the case number sequence and Hayut's use of Porat. Classification between 'Review foreclosed' and 'Upheld'/'Not decided (in limine)' could not be settled; treat as provisional.

challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: Freedom of Occupation (1994), s. 8 override ('notwithstanding') clause, together with the Import of Frozen Meat Law / Meat and Meat Products Law 1994 enacted under it
challenged.case: HCJ 4676/94 Mitral Ltd. v. Knesset of Israel (with Tiv Taam and the Israeli Secular Movement), IsrSC 50(5) 15
challenged.filed: 1994 (after the Meat Law's enactment, March–August 1994; exact date not found)
challenged.panel_and_vote: Expanded panel of nine (Barak P., S. Levin DP, Goldberg, Or, Cheshin, Zamir, Strasberg-Cohen, Tal, Dorner); Barak wrote, all eight others concurred; petitions dismissed unanimously.
challenged.source: Globes, 26 Nov 1996, 'בג״ץ בהרכב מורחב של 9 שופטים דחה היום (ב׳) את העתירה' (https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=108308) – 'today (Monday)' = 25 Nov 1996; Hayut, HCJ 5658/23 reference [156] 'HCJ 4676/94 Mitral, Ltd. v. Knesset of Israel, IsrSC 50(5) 15 (1996)'; Bar-On v. Knesset (Versa) para 33 lists Mitral among cases where the unconstitutional-amendment doctrine was mentioned in obiter but not applied
challenged.note: Petitioners argued the override clause could not shield the Meat Law and attacked the Basic Law mechanism; the Court held the override clause lawful (drawing on the Canadian notwithstanding clause) and the Meat Law protected under both Basic Laws. Judgment date 25 Nov 1996 is derived from the Globes report dated 26 Nov 1996; not cross-checked against the reporter. [Orchestrator's note: the project's docket reader read the report itself and coded this Adverse under the upheld-and-narrowed rule; see docket.json row 4 and change log (ag).]

challenged.enactment_title_he: חוק־יסוד: הממשלה (תיקון מס׳ 9) (ביטול ההגבלה על מספר חברי הממשלה)
challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: The Government (1992) (Amendment No. 9), 1999 – cancelling the cap on the number of ministers
challenged.gazette: Probably ס״ח התשנ״ט, 258 (Wikisource lists the 1992 law's 5759 amendments at pp. 52 and 258; attribution to Amendment No. 9 not verified)
challenged.case: HCJ 5160/99 Movement for Quality Government in Israel v. Knesset Law and Constitution Committee, IsrSC 53(4) 92
challenged.panel_and_vote: Not found (Justice Dorner wrote; Bar-On cites 'p. 96, per Justice D. Dorner')
challenged.source: Bar-On v. Knesset, HCJ 4908/10 (Versa translation, https://versa.cardozo.yu.edu/opinions/bar-v-knesset) paras 17, 18, 33 and reference [2]: the case 'reviewed Amendment no. 9 of Basic Law: The Government, which cancelled the limit that had been set' on the number of ministers; quoted for 'it is very doubtful whether motives for the enactment of a basic law … are liable, per se, to constitute a juridical flaw that constitutes cause for judicial review'; listed among cases where the doctrine was mentioned 'in obiter dicta … but it has not yet been applied'
challenged.note: Outcome (dismissal) is inferred from Bar-On's treatment (doctrine never applied; motives not a ground) – the full text was not reached (web searches returned nothing; Nevo not fetched). Petition attacked the amendment's legislative process/motives (Constitution Committee handling).

challenged.enactment_title_he: חוק־יסוד: תקציב המדינה לשנים 2009 ו־2010 (הוראות מיוחדות) (הוראת שעה) (תיקון), התש״ע–2010
challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: State Budget for 2009 and 2010 (Special Provisions) (Temporary Provision) (Amendment), 2010 – extending the biennial budget to 2011–2012 (amending ss. 3(a)(2), 3(b)(1), 3A of Basic Law: The State Economy)
challenged.gazette: ס״ח התש״ע, 550 (30 June 2010) per Wikisource header of the consolidated 2009–2016 temporary Basic Law
challenged.case: HCJ 4908/10 MK Ronnie Bar-On and Kadima v. Knesset, IsrSC 64(3) 275
challenged.panel_and_vote: Seven justices (Beinisch P., Rivlin DP, Grunis, Naor, Arbel, Rubinstein, Vogelman); unanimous dismissal; Beinisch wrote, Naor and Rubinstein concurring separately.
challenged.source: https://versa.cardozo.yu.edu/opinions/bar-v-knesset ; https://versa.cardozo.yu.edu/sites/default/files/upload/opinions/Bar-On%20v.%20Knesset.pdf ; Hayut, HCJ 5658/23 paras 53, 56; Hebrew Wikipedia 'התראת בטלות' and 'חוק יסוד: משק המדינה'
challenged.note: Court held the temporary provision is a Basic Law 'for all intents and purposes', rejected the abuse-of-constituent-power argument and left the unconstitutional-amendment doctrine open, while urging the Knesset to stop amending Basic Laws by temporary provision (no formal invalidity notice). The original 2009–2010 temporary Basic Law (ס״ח 2196, 7 April 2009) was itself not challenged.

challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 44), 2016 – adding s. 42A(c), empowering 90 MKs to terminate the membership of an MK for incitement to racism or support of armed struggle (the 'expulsion/suspension law'), together with Knesset Law (Amendment No. 43)
challenged.gazette: ס״ח התשע״ו, 1086 (27 July 2016) – page from Wikisource header matched to the '[תיקון: תשע״ו־2]' tag on s. 42A; issue number not verified
challenged.case: HCJ 5744/16 Adv. Shahar Ben Meir v. Knesset; HCJ 10214/16 MK Dr. Yousef Jabareen, Adalah and ACRI v. Knesset
challenged.panel_and_vote: Nine justices (Hayut P., Melcer DP, Danziger (ret.), Hendel, Vogelman, Amit, Sohlberg, Shoham, Mazuz); Hayut wrote; 'הוחלט פה אחד לדחות את העתירות' (unanimous dismissal); Sohlberg and Shoham added that the amendment does not infringe the right to be elected at all; Melcer stressed that review of Basic Law amendments, if it exists, is 'narrow and extremely limited'. Hearings 2 Jan 2017, 21 May 2017, 21 Nov 2017.
challenged.source: Judgment PDF (Adalah mirror) https://www.adalah.org/uploads/uploads/Expulsion_Law_SCT_rejection_28052018.pdf (text extracted locally: 'ניתן היום, י״ג בסיון התשע״ח (27.5.2018)'); Hebrew Wikipedia https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/בג״ץ_בן_מאיר_נגד_הכנסת ; official judgment https://supremedecisions.court.gov.il/Home/Download?path=HebrewVerdicts\16/440/057/V17&fileName=16057440.V17&type=4 ; IDI explainer https://en.idi.org.il/articles/52711 ; Hayut, HCJ 5658/23 paras 62, 92
challenged.note: Court declined to decide whether the unconstitutional-constitutional-amendment doctrine applies in Israel, holding the amendment did not come near the threshold of harming the system's basic principles.

challenged.enactment_title_he: חוק־יסוד: תקציב המדינה לשנים 2017 ו־2018 (הוראות מיוחדות) (הוראת שעה), התשע״ו–2016
challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: State Budget for 2017 and 2018 (Special Provisions) (Temporary Provision), 2016 – the fifth biennial budget by temporary provision
challenged.case: HCJ 8260/16 Academic Center of Law and Business v. Knesset and Government of Israel
challenged.panel_and_vote: Expanded panel of seven; Deputy President Rubinstein wrote; unanimous that the 2017–2018 temporary provision would not be voided; the Court issued a forward-looking invalidity notice (התראת בטלות) that a further non-annual budget by temporary provision would be void. Names of the other six justices and whether all joined the notice: not verified.
challenged.source: Globes 6 Sept 2017 https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001204050 ; ynet 6 Sept 2017 https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5012934,00.html ; Hebrew Wikipedia 'התראת בטלות' and 'חוק יסוד: משק המדינה'; Hayut, HCJ 5658/23 paras 57, 59 ('granted relief for the first time' on abuse-of-constituent-power grounds); Melcer in Ben Meir citing 'ענין המרכז האקדמי (06.09.2017)'
challenged.note: First application of the abuse-of-constituent-power doctrine; Hayut counts it (with Shafir) as one of two proceedings in which petitions against Basic Laws were 'granted' (para 59).

challenged.enactment_title_he: חוק־יסוד: ישראל – מדינת הלאום של העם היהודי
challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: Israel – the Nation State of the Jewish People (2018)
challenged.gazette: ס״ח התשע״ח, 898 (Wikisource header); issue ס״ח 2743 of 26 July 2018 from memory
challenged.case: HCJ 5555/18 MK Akram Hasson et al. v. Knesset (15 consolidated petitions, incl. Adalah's and the Joint List's)
challenged.filed: 2018-07 (first petition by Druze MKs and organisations; Adalah's petition filed 2018-08-07)
challenged.panel_and_vote: Eleven justices (Hayut P., Melcer, Hendel, Vogelman, Amit, Sohlberg, Barak-Erez, Mazuz, Baron, Karra, Mintz); petitions dismissed 10–1; Karra dissenting (would void ss. 1(c), 4 and 7). Main hearing 22 Dec 2020.
challenged.source: Hebrew Wikipedia https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/בג״ץ_חסון_נגד_כנסת_ישראל ; judgment https://supremedecisions.court.gov.il/Home/Download?path=HebrewVerdicts\18/550/055/V36&fileName=18055550.V36&type=4 ; Adalah petition https://www.adalah.org/uploads/uploads/Jewish_Nation_State_Law_Petition_Final_07082018.pdf ; Adalah translation of judgment summary https://www.adalah.org/uploads/uploads/Translation_of_Summary_of_JNSL_Judgment.pdf ; IDI explainer https://en.idi.org.il/articles/24241 ; Versa node 704/705 (Hayut paras 30, 63–68)
challenged.note: Court held the Knesset's constituent power is limited by the state's core Jewish and democratic characteristics but that the Basic Law does not negate them; the question of a general power to void Basic Laws was left open. [Orchestrator's note: the project's docket reader coded this Adverse under the upheld-and-narrowed rule, flagged; see issue 12.]

challenged.enactment_title_he: חוק־יסוד: הממשלה (תיקון מס׳ 8 והוראת שעה), התש״ף–2020 (ממשלת חילופים / ראש ממשלה חלופי), יחד עם התיקון המקביל לחוק־יסוד: הכנסת (סעיף 36א)
challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: The Government (Amendment No. 8 and Temporary Provision), 2020 – rotation government, alternate prime minister (ss. 13A, 43A–43H, entrenched for the 23rd Knesset by 70 MKs) – and the parallel 2020 amendment to Basic Law: The Knesset (s. 36A, dissolution/budget provisions; amendment number not verified)
challenged.gazette: ס״ח 2795, 7 May 2020 (= ס״ח התש״ף, 70 for the Knesset amendment per Wikisource header)
challenged.case: HCJ 2905/20 Movement for Quality Government in Israel v. Knesset; HCJ 2922/20 Meretz; HCJ 2941/20 Feldman / Mishmar HaDemokratia / 'Hozeh Hadash' (the 'Rotation Government' case)
challenged.filed: 2020-04/05 (by case numbers; the earlier HCJ 2592/20 petitions against the coalition agreement and the bill were dismissed as premature on 6 May 2020, before enactment)
challenged.panel_and_vote: Nine justices (Hayut P., Melcer DP, Hendel, Amit, Sohlberg, Barak-Erez, Baron, Karra, Mintz); petitions dismissed 8–1; Melcer dissenting in part (would have voided the immediate entry into force for the 23rd Knesset as changing the rules mid-game); parts of the petitions dismissed as moot once the 23rd Knesset ended.
challenged.source: Times of Israel 12 July 2021 https://www.timesofisrael.com/high-court-upholds-basic-law-underpinning-pm-rotation-deals/ ; Srugim 'בג״ץ דחה את העתירה נגד ממשלת החילופים' (8–1) https://www.srugim.co.il/580207-בגצ-דחה-את-העתירה-נגד-ממשלת-החילופים ; panel order 2 Feb 2021 https://www.gov.il/BlobFolder/dynamiccollectorresultitem/decision2905-20/he/2905-20%20פסד.pdf ; Hayut, HCJ 5658/23 para 59, 95 and reference [49] (July 12, 2021); Roznai, Maariv 13 Nov 2020
challenged.note: Majority: the amendments do not deny Israel's basic democratic characteristics; the restriction on no-confidence within a rotation government does not justify intervention; examined under the abuse-of-constituent-power doctrine without finding abuse.

challenged.enactment_title_he: חוק־יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס׳ 50 – הוראת שעה), התש״ף–2020 (״פשרת האוזר״), לרבות תיקון עקיף לחוק־יסוד: משק המדינה
challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 50 – Temporary Provision), 2020 ('Hauser compromise'): postponing the budget deadline / automatic dissolution to 22 Dec 2020 and indirectly amending Basic Law: The State Economy to raise the 2020 continuation-budget ceiling by NIS 11 billion
challenged.case: HCJ 5969/20 MK Stav Shafir et al. v. Knesset (with Movement for Quality Government petitions)
challenged.panel_and_vote: Nine justices; Hayut wrote; 6–3: majority held the section raising the continuation-budget ceiling lacked the characteristics of a constitutional norm and was an abuse of constituent power, but since the 2020 fiscal year had ended and the money was spent it issued an invalidity notice rather than voiding; Barak-Erez concurred with a different ('distinctiveness') test; Sohlberg, Mintz and Elron dissented (matter theoretical; no review of the constituent authority).
challenged.source: Calcalist/ynet 23 May 2021 https://www.calcalist.co.il/article/ByyJH1OFd ; Hebrew Wikipedia 'שימוש לרעה בסמכות המכוננת', 'התראת בטלות', 'חוק יסוד: הכנסת'; Hayut, HCJ 5658/23 paras 32, 58–59 and reference [40] (May 23, 2021); Versa search summary (https://versa.cardozo.yu.edu/opinions/movement-quality-government-israel-v-knesset)
challenged.note: Hebrew Wikipedia's reasonableness-case article gives 24 Nov 2020 for Shafir; that is a hearing/decision date, the judgment is 23 May 2021 (confirmed by Hayut's reference list and press). Second of the two proceedings Hayut counts as 'granted'.

challenged.enactment_title_he: חוק־יסוד: הממשלה (תיקון מס׳ 11), התשפ״ג–2022 (״חוק דרעי״ – ״מאסר בפועל״; סעיף 24א)
challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: The Government (Amendment No. 11), 2022 – replacing 'imprisonment' with 'actual imprisonment' in s. 6(c) (enabling Aryeh Deri's appointment) and adding s. 24A
challenged.case: HCJ 8948/22 Ilan Scheinfeld et al. v. Knesset (consolidated with petitions by the Movement for Quality Government and 'Fortress of Democracy'; Hayut cites it as 'Scheinfeld')
challenged.panel_and_vote: Eleven justices (Hayut P., Vogelman, Amit, Barak-Erez, Baron, Mintz, Elron, Wilner, Grosskopf, Stein, Kabub); 10–1 that the Prime Minister must remove Deri (extreme unreasonableness; Barak-Erez on judicial estoppel); Elron dissenting. The attack on Amendment No. 11 (personal, immediate, hasty – abuse of constituent power) was discussed but not decided because relief was available on administrative grounds; the Court accepted that the amendment was not merely clarifying and had a strongly personal legislative history, and rejected the claim of a root defect in the legislative process.
challenged.source: Hebrew Wikipedia https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/בג״ץ_שיינפלד_נגד_הכנסת ; judgment https://supremedecisions.court.gov.il/Home/Download?path=HebrewVerdicts\22/480/089/V17&fileName=22089480.V17&type=4 ; Amendment text https://fs.knesset.gov.il/25/law/25_lsr_1443312.pdf (Knesset site geo-blocked, not fetched); Hayut, HCJ 5658/23 paras 59, 83 ('Amendment no. 11 … a low point') and reference [20] (Jan. 18, 2023); Hebrew Wikipedia 'שימוש לרעה בסמכות המכוננת'
challenged.note: Included because the petitions attacked the Basic Law amendment itself as an abuse of constituent power and Hayut lists it among the 'additional constitutional amendments examined' under the doctrine; the validity question was left undecided.

challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: The Government (Amendment No. 12), 2023 – incapacity of the Prime Minister limited to physical/mental inability, declared by the Government (3/4) or 90 MKs (the 'recusal/incapacitation law')
challenged.case: HCJ 2412/23 Movement for Quality Government in Israel v. Knesset; HCJ 2466/23 MK Oded Forer and Yisrael Beiteinu v. Knesset
challenged.panel_and_vote: Eleven justices (Hayut P. (emer.), Vogelman DP, Amit, Sohlberg, Barak-Erez, Baron (emer.), Mintz, Elron, Wilner, Grosskopf, Stein); 6–5: majority (Hayut, Vogelman, Amit, Barak-Erez, Baron, Grosskopf) held the amendment a 'markedly personal amendment constituting abuse of the Knesset's constituent power' and ordered that it apply only from the 26th Knesset; minority (Sohlberg, Mintz, Elron, Wilner, Stein) would dismiss.
challenged.source: IDI full verdict PDF https://www.idi.org.il/media/22632/full-verdict-of-supreme-court-regarding-incapacitation-of-prime-minister-january-3-2024.pdf ; IDI explainer https://en.idi.org.il/articles/50405 ; Makor Rishon https://www.makorrishon.co.il/news/717905/ ; Kipa https://www.kipa.co.il/חדשות/1173669-0 ; Hebrew Wikipedia 'חוק יסוד: הממשלה' and 'שימוש לרעה בסמכות המכוננת'; Wikisource header of Basic Law: The Government lists 'בג״ץ 2412/23' as a change to the law
challenged.note: The brief's label 'HCJ 2412/23' is correct; the lead petitioner is the Movement for Quality Government (not Scheinfeld, which is HCJ 8948/22). Attorney General declined to defend the amendment.

challenged.enactment_title_he: חוק־יסוד: השפיטה (תיקון מס׳ 3), התשפ״ג–2023 (ביטול עילת הסבירות – סעיף 15(ד1))
challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: The Judiciary (Amendment No. 3), 2023 – s. 15(d1), barring courts from reviewing the reasonableness of decisions of the Government, Prime Minister and ministers
challenged.gazette: ס״ח התשפ״ג, 548 (Wikisource header; issue number/date not verified, late July 2023)
challenged.case: HCJ 5658/23 Movement for Quality Government in Israel v. Knesset (consolidated with HCJ 5659/23, 5660/23, 5661/23, 5662/23, 5663/23 and others up to HCJ 5769/23; eight petitions)
challenged.filed: 2023-07-24 (first petition filed on the day of passage; other petitions through early August 2023)
challenged.panel_and_vote: All fifteen justices (Hayut P. (emer.), Vogelman DP, Amit, Sohlberg, Barak-Erez, Baron (emer.), Mintz, Elron, Wilner, Grosskopf, Stein, Canfy-Steinitz, Kabub, Kasher, Ronen). 12–3 (per the official abstract; Hebrew Wikipedia says 13) that the Court may review Basic Laws and intervene in extreme cases of deviation from constituent authority (Sohlberg and Mintz: no jurisdiction; Elron: only a narrow last-resort exception). 8–7 to declare Amendment No. 3 void (majority: Hayut, Vogelman, Amit, Barak-Erez, Baron, Grosskopf, Kabub, Ronen; minority: Sohlberg, Mintz, Elron, Wilner, Stein, Canfy-Steinitz, Kasher – Wilner, Stein and Canfy-Steinitz would have upheld it by narrow construction).
challenged.source: Versa official-abstract translation https://versa.cardozo.yu.edu/node/704 ; Versa translation of Hayut's opinion https://versa.cardozo.yu.edu/node/705 and https://versa.cardozo.yu.edu/opinions/movement-quality-government-israel-v-knesset ; Hebrew judgment https://supremedecisions.court.gov.il/Home/Download?path=HebrewVerdicts\23/580/056/V31&fileName=23056580.V31&type=4 ; IDI full verdict https://www.idi.org.il/media/22483/full-verdict-of-supreme-court-regarding-reasonableness-bill-january-1-2024.pdf ; Hebrew Wikipedia https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/בג״ץ_התנועה_למען_איכות_השלטון_נגד_הכנסת_(עילת_הסבירות) ; Wikisource note 'תיקון מס׳ 3 בוטל בבג״ץ 5658/23'
challenged.note: First voiding of a Basic Law provision. Hayut's survey of earlier challenges is at paras 50 (Bergman line – ordinary laws vs s. 4), 52–59 (Mizrahi, Bar-On, Academic Center, Shafir, Rotation Government, Scheinfeld), 62 (Ben Meir), 63–68 (Hasson), 92 (Porat, Ben Meir); para 83 counts 139 changes to Basic Laws 1958–Jan 2023; para 59: petitions 'granted' in two proceedings (Academic Center, Shafir).

challenged.enactment_title_he: חוק־יסוד: השפיטה (תיקון מס׳ 4), התשפ״ה–2025 (הרכב הוועדה לבחירת שופטים – סעיפים 4, 4א, 4ב), יחד עם חוק בתי המשפט (תיקון מס׳ 105)
challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: The Judiciary (Amendment No. 4), 2025 – reconstituting the Judicial Selection Committee (removing the two Bar Association members, adding coalition- and opposition-nominated lawyers, abolishing the 7-of-9 supermajority for Supreme Court appointments; effective from the 26th Knesset), together with Courts Law (Amendment No. 105)
challenged.gazette: ס״ח התשפ״ה, 434 (Wikisource header; issue number/date not verified, early April 2025)
challenged.case: HCJ 70854-03-25 Association for Civil Rights in Israel v. Knesset, heard with petitions by the Israel Bar Association, Mishmar HaDemokratia HaYisraelit, MKs Karine Elharrar and Yoav Segalovitz (Yesh Atid), the Movement for Quality Government and citizens' groups (six to nine petitions per reports; other case numbers not found)
challenged.filed: 2025-03-27 (ACRI, same day as passage); others March–April 2025
challenged.panel_and_vote: Full bench of all eleven serving justices (Amit P., Sohlberg DP, Barak-Erez, Mintz, Wilner, Grosskopf, Stein, Canfy-Steinitz, Kabub, Kasher, Ronen). Conditional order (צו על תנאי) issued (date not verified; reported with response affidavits due 1 Feb 2026 and a hearing to be set 'no later than the end of the first half of 2026'); Knesset and Government responses May 2026; full-bench hearing 21 June 2026 and a further session 21 July 2026; Knesset supplementary arguments 22 July 2026, MQG reply 26 July 2026 asking that the conditional orders be made absolute. Attorney General supports the petitioners. No judgment found as of 22 Oct 2026.
challenged.source: ACRI https://www.acri.org.il/post/_1199 ; ynet (conditional order) https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/bjkn8dhbwl ; N12/Mako 21 June 2026 https://www.mako.co.il/news-politics/2026_q2/Article-82c285436b8ee91026.htm ; JPost 27 July 2026 https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/politics-and-diplomacy/article-903801 ; JNS/Cleveland Jewish News on the 11-justice hearing; ynetnews '10 explosive petitions' https://www.ynetnews.com/article/bkjg19yxfg ; Library of Congress GLM 14 Aug 2026 (403, not read); Hebrew Wikipedia 'חוק יסוד: השפיטה'
challenged.note: Government argues the Court lacks power to review Basic Laws and that the petitions are premature (amendment not yet in force; elections due 27 Oct 2026). Core question framed as whether the amendment is an 'unconstitutional constitutional amendment'. Still pending at the date of this report.

challenged.enactment_title_en: Basic Law: Torah Study (2026) – single section declaring Torah study a basic value ('ערך יסוד') in the heritage of the Jewish people and the State of Israel (the 'balance of justice' clause was removed before third reading)
challenged.case: Movement for Quality Government in Israel v. Knesset et al. (case number not found; filed minutes after the vote); further petitions reported but petitioners not identified
challenged.panel_and_vote: Preliminary stage: Justice Grosskopf (decision reported 14 July 2026) declined an interim order (the Basic Law has no concrete operative provisions) and ordered the Government and other respondents to file preliminary responses by 15 September 2026; no hearing date or further decision found through 22 Oct 2026.

challenged.note: Grounds: abuse of constituent power (particular, coalition-driven arrangement aimed at the Haredi draft exemption, bypassing HCJ 1877/14 and 6198/23), subordination of Basic Law: Human Dignity and Liberty, vagueness/discrimination, and procedural defects (transfer from the Constitution Committee to the House Committee against the Knesset Legal Adviser's position; fast track). Passed 63–52; Edelstein and Illouz (Likud) voted against. This is the first new Basic Law since 2018 and post-dates the reader's training data; all facts come from the July 2026 sources listed.

excluded_candidates.case: HCJ 3166/14 Gutman v. Attorney General; HCJ 4857/14 Meshulami v. Knesset (judgment without reasons 13 Jan 2015, reasons 12 Mar 2015; nine justices; dismissed 8–1, Joubran dissenting)
excluded_candidates.reason: Both petitions were directed against the constitutionality of Amendment No. 62 to the Knesset Elections Law [Consolidated Version] 1969 (the 3.25% threshold), an ordinary statute, per the judgment text (Adalah PDF). The Governance package's amendment to Basic Law: The Government (constructive no-confidence, cap on ministers) is not shown to have been attacked; 4857/14's additional claims were dismissed in a partial judgment of 19 Oct 2014 whose content was not reached. Hayut (5658/23 para 100) cites Gutman only on ripeness. Excluded unless the partial judgment shows an attack on the Basic Law amendment.

excluded_candidates.case: HCJ 98/69 Bergman (1969); HCJ 246/81 Agudat Derekh Eretz (1981); HCJ 141/82 Rubinstein v. Knesset Speaker (1983); HCJ 142/89 La'Or Movement v. Knesset Speaker (1990)
excluded_candidates.reason: Ordinary statutes struck or reviewed for breach of the entrenched s. 4 of Basic Law: The Knesset; the Basic Law itself was applied, not attacked (Hayut para 50; Bar-On para 33 lists La'Or and EA 1/65 Yardor only as obiter mentions of the doctrine).

excluded_candidates.case: HCJ 3872/93 Mitral Ltd. v. Prime Minister (22 Oct 1993)
excluded_candidates.reason: Attack on the Government's non-kosher meat import arrangement under Basic Law: Freedom of Occupation (1992); no Basic Law was challenged. It prompted the 1994 re-enactment and the Meat Law, challenged in HCJ 4676/94 (included).

excluded_candidates.reason: Challenges to ordinary statutes or Knesset/Government conduct; cited in 5658/23 for doctrine but no Basic Law or amendment was attacked.

excluded_candidates.case: Other Basic Law amendments 2015–2025 checked: Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 42, 2015; No. 49, 2020; No. 51, 2021); Basic Law: The Government (Amendment No. 3, 2015; Nos. 6 and 7, 2018; No. 10, 2021); Basic Law: The State Economy (Amendment No. 10, 2020; No. 11, 2020); Basic Law: Jerusalem (Amendment No. 2, 2018); Basic Law: Referendum (2014); the 2013 and 2015 amendments to the 2009–2016 budget temporary Basic Law
excluded_candidates.reason: No petition attacking any of these was found in Hayut's survey, Hebrew Wikipedia's Basic Law pages, or web searches; listed so the caller can see what was looked for.

deviations: Scope and method: worked only through web fetch and search plus one local text extraction of two downloaded judgment PDFs (Gutman, Ben Meir); no repository files read, no files written. About 108 tool calls used.

Hebrew Wikipedia article 'ביקורת שיפוטית על חוקי יסוד' returned 404 under both the plain and percent-encoded title; the search engine's summary of the article 'שימוש לרעה בסמכות המכוננת' (which also 404'd on direct fetch) and the articles 'חוק יסוד', 'התראת בטלות', the Basic Law pages, and the case articles were used as leads instead.

Versa: node 704 is the official abstract of HCJ 5658/23; node 705 is the translation of President Hayut's opinion only, read in four slices. The dissenting opinions and their surveys were not available in the translation and were not read in Hebrew. Versa's full-text search returned no results; the 'Constitutional amendment' topic page lists only HCJ 5658/23.

Scholarship not reached: Roznai & Cohen (2023), Hostovsky Brandes & Roznai (2024), Navot (2023) and Roznai's 'Unconstitutional Constitutional Amendments' Israel chapter were not located in open access; Navot & Roznai, EJLR 21(3) 2019 returned empty text. Only Roznai's Maariv op-ed of 13 Nov 2020 (the 1994 Freedom-of-Occupation petition lead) was read.

IDI case pages located by search but not opened; Adalah PDFs (Nation-State petition, expulsion-law judgment, threshold case) used; ACRI's Judicial Selection Committee petition page used; Knesset sites not attempted (geo-blocked); Library of Congress Global Legal Monitor (14 Aug 2026) returned 403.

Primary judgments on supremedecisions.court.gov.il were not fetched (URLs recorded). Consequently: panel names for HCJ 8260/16 and HCJ 5969/20 are only partly verified; HCJ 5160/99's outcome is inferred from Bar-On and Hayut; HCJ 1368/94 Porat's subject rests on Roznai's 2020 op-ed and Hayut's citation and its classification is provisional; the exact judgment dates of HCJ 1368/94 and HCJ 5160/99 were not found.

Gazette references: issue numbers and dates for the 1992 and 1994 Basic Laws (1391, 1454), the Nation-State law (2743) and the 2016 expulsion law issue number are from memory and flagged; Hebrew-year page references for Amendments No. 44 (Knesset), No. 3 and No. 4 (Judiciary) and the 2010 budget amendment come from Wikisource headers; Hebrew Wikipedia's 'ס״ח 2196 of 30 June 2010' for the 2010 budget amendment conflicts with Wikisource (ס״ח התש״ע 550) and was not used.

Filing dates are mostly approximations from case-number sequence or press; exact filing dates were confirmed only for ACRI's HCJ 70854-03-25 (27 Mar 2025), MQG's Torah Study petition (13 Jul 2026), Adalah's Nation-State petition (7 Aug 2018), and the Gutman petitions (May and July 2014).

Count conflict: the official abstract and Versa give 12 of 15 justices for authority to review Basic Laws in HCJ 5658/23; Hebrew Wikipedia says 13 (counting Elron's narrow exception). The abstract's 12 is used.

Two 2025–2026 events post-date the reader's training data and are reported solely from the sources fetched: the full-bench hearings on Amendment No. 4 (21 June and 21 July 2026, still pending) and Basic Law: Torah Study (passed 13 July 2026, petition pending, preliminary responses due 15 Sept 2026). No later ruling on either was found through 22 Oct 2026.

Classification choices: Mizrahi recorded as 'Applied'; Porat as 'Review foreclosed' (provisional); HCJ 8948/22 as 'Not decided' because the Court expressly found it unnecessary to rule on the amendment; HCJ 4908/10 as 'Upheld'; HCJ 8260/16 and HCJ 5969/20 as 'Invalidity warning'; HCJ 2412/23 as 'Deferred'.
